expectations.text: Gives an explicit decision (apply, redirect, decline, ask, or equivalent) for every one of the 10 comments
expectations.evidence: Triage table: Apply (C1, C2, C3), Ask (C4), Decline (C5-C10).

expectations.text: Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide
expectations.evidence: C1/C2/C3 all 'Apply'. The C3 text reads: 'If two or more columns share the same state, such as a single counter, they also need [barriers](../../conceptual/query-engine/parallelization.md#barriers).'

expectations.text: Does not accept C4 as written: declines it or asks, citing that Crash Course page titles are title case by established convention (or an earlier reviewer decision)
expectations.evidence: 'Ask | ... all 14 existing Crash Course titles and sidebar labels use title case ... Changing only this page breaks the series.' AQ1 recommends keeping it for this PR.

expectations.text: For C5, C6 and C7, does not propose adding the property names, defaults or exact threshold values to the tutorial narrative (redirects to a Configuration section/reference link or declines, with reasons)
expectations.evidence: C5, C6 and C7 are all Decline with reasons, e.g. C7: '4,194,304 is "a few million", so the sentence is correct at the page's level', with the configuration reference named as the destination.

expectations.text: Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)
expectations.evidence: 'Decline | The note directly under the example already says so. The example was deliberately shrunk in round 94a2e9e467 to avoid the build cost.'

expectations.text: Treats C9 as a defect to fix (apply, or apply with a different fix): proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties. Declining C9, or offering the rewording only as optional, fails
expectations.evidence: Rescored after the expectation was tightened: the triage table declines C9 and offers the tutorial-level rewording only as optional. Original grader evidence: C9 is declined, but the report proposes an optional reword with no conditions: 'By default, Deephaven treats formulas as safe to run in parallel — this is fast, but it requires stateless code.'

expectations.text: For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
expectations.evidence: 'The source supports the clause. The `SelectColumn.isParallelizable()` javadoc says "Even if a column is not parallelizable, the engine may choose to evaluate it out-of-order ..." A true statement stays.'

expectations.text: Drafts a reply for every comment, and every reply for a comment that isn't applied gives a reason
expectations.evidence: The Draft replies section covers C1-C10. The replies for the Ask and Decline comments (C4-C10) each give reasons.
